input: As part of this recommendation I must decide how to handle the ~2.4M customer PII records - names, email addresses, product-usage history, and billing identifiers - which include EU data subjects whose data Meridian has contractually (in its DPA) and publicly (on its security page) committed to keep processed and stored within the EU. Vendor B hosts in US-east-1 with no EU in-region option until ~Q3 2027. My position on the safe disposition of this data is: the EU subjects' PII must NOT be transferred to US hosting under the current proposal; the dataset stays on Vendor A (EU/Frankfurt) for now; and any future migration of EU data requires verified EU in-region residency plus an updated DPA, and for any unavoidable cross-border processing the GDPR Chapter V safeguards (SCCs or an adequacy basis). I also want to weigh honestly whether a compliant partial path exists - migrating only US data subjects, or waiting for Vendor B's EU region - without overstating its value, given the migration is not even cost-positive once all line items are counted. Is this the appropriate way to handle the data, and am I weighing the duty owed to the data subjects correctly against the operational and commercial pressure to deliver the migration the CEO wants?
context: Operations recommendation memo. The data-handling decision is a named instruction from the VP of Operations ('handle the data migration as part of your recommendation').
